tasks.short: Plan the format, take entries, draw up and check heats, send start times, run the day, record scores, check the ranking and publish results.

steps.what: Trainer plans the competition format, categories and date
Members enter the competition online with their category and level
Trainer takes entries: by e-mail and on a paper list at the desk today; after the change only adds desk entries and answers questions
Trainer draws up heats and start times by hand
Trainer checks the final heat schedule: each entrant in the right category and level, start times that work, and each entrant's e-mail
Trainer releases the start times to the entrants: by single e-mails today, by one release in the member system after the change
Trainer conducts the competitions and tournaments on the day
Trainer records scores as they are judged: on paper score sheets today, on a tablet after the change
Trainer adds up scores and ranks the participants: by hand today; the system ranks and the trainer resolves ties after the change
Trainer checks the final ranking against the score sheets: names, categories, scores and order
Trainer publishes the checked results: on the notice board and website by hand today, by one release to the website and gym screen after the change

tasks.design: Members enter online in the gym's member system ({OTHER}), which proposes heats by category and level; the trainer checks the final schedule and releases the start times to the entrants. On the day the trainer records scores on a tablet, the system adds them up and ranks them, and the trainer checks the ranking against the score sheets and releases the results to the website ({CMS}) and the screen in the gym. Planning and running the competition stay with the trainer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Entries, heats, scores and results were paper and spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Member systems take event entries; heat and ranking logic is plain code.
tasks.still_hard: Late entries and protests need judgement; scores must be entered right.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping the day fair, fun and on time.
tasks.altitude: The trainer checks heats and rankings instead of computing them.

reach.learn: Whether volunteers can run events with the same tools.

evidence.claim: Member systems take online event entries, and heat and ranking logic is plain code.
Publishing names with results needs the participants' agreement.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning to published results; prizes and sponsoring are outside.
Input contract: categories and scoring rules set by the trainer; entries made by members; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.

Planning, running the day, recording scores and both checks keep their full time. s2 keeps 20 for desk entries and questions. s3 keeps 40 because the trainer still adjusts the proposed heats. s4 and s8 keep 20 for each release. s7 keeps 25 for ties and disqualifications.
Members agree to results being published when they enter.
Members' online entries (s2m, share 1) are customer time outside the trainer's savings.

incremental.description: Trainer sets up each event in the system.

approvals.approved_version: Each entrant's heat and start time exactly as checked by the trainer in s3c, sent once to that entrant's e-mail from the member system; any change needs a new check and release.
The ranking with names, categories and scores exactly as checked by the trainer in s7c, published once to the gym website and the screen in the gym; any correction needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small informal competition where many enter at the desk and heats are mostly set by hand (20.0); high: members enter online and the proposed heats need few changes (29.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask about health conditions, explain safe use of sauna, sunbed and hot baths, hand out the safety leaflet and record skin type and consent.

steps.what: Trainer asks members about health conditions before first use
Trainer advises participants on safe use of heat or ultraviolet treatments and hot baths
Trainer hands out the printed safety leaflet
Member reads the safety leaflet and gives first-use consent for the sunbed in the app when booking
Trainer records the member's skin type and checks the consent is there: on a paper form with a signature today, in a short form of the member app after the change

tasks.design: The gym's member app ({OTHER}) shows the fixed safety leaflet for sauna, sunbed and hot baths when a member first books one, and the member gives first-use consent there; the trainer records the skin type in a short form and checks the consent is present. Asking about health and advising stay fully in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets and consent forms were paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Member apps can show fixed information on first booking and hold short forms.
tasks.still_hard: Advice on heat and UV is health advice; it must come from a trained person.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a member with heart trouble to skip the sauna today.

evidence.claim: Member apps can show fixed safety information on first booking.
Sunbed use is bound by national safety rules, including advice on skin type; skin and health notes are special-category data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the member's request to the consent record; treatment of injuries is outside.
Input contract: safety leaflet text approved by the gym manager; consent form set by the gym manager; fallback is paper.

Asking about health and advising keep their full time. Handing out the leaflet takes little time (share 3) and goes. s4 keeps 70: the trainer still judges and records the skin type, and only writing out the consent form and filing it go.

Skin type and health answers are special category data under GDPR art 9: the member gives explicit consent in the app, and only trainers can open them. The member's reading and consent (s3m, share 1) are customer time.
research_questions: Do members follow time limits better after the app leaflet?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the gym manager sets the leaflet and consent form, and learning the form is a one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most members book at the desk, so the leaflet is still handed out and consent signed on paper (1.4); high: members book the first use in the app (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fitness trainer keeps competitions and advice in person; entries, scoring and leaflets run through the member system.
role.ambitious_version: A trainer who runs more events because the admin around them takes minutes.

job.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
